character:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: original character exploration sheet for a Twitch gameplay entertainment companion, a best friend on the couch. Create one polished landscape 3:2 art-director presentation board, not a collage of screenshots.
Primary request: compare exactly three original small animated companion designs in three clean horizontal rows, with four distinct readable emotional poses per design. The consistent column headings are "WATCHING", "HYPED", "SKEPTICAL", "OOPS". Clear text labels at the left of each row are "01  ORB", "02  SPRITE", "03  POCKET BOT".
Subject design: ORB is a charming moss-green little rounded pebble/orb, cream face area, thick graphite expressive brows, tiny terracotta mitten hands and little feet; no ears or familiar franchise silhouette. SPRITE is a small original forest spirit with cream circular head, short moss leaf cloak and two asymmetrical simple foliage tufts, terracotta scarf, tiny boots; friendly but impish, not a human fairy and no wings. POCKET BOT is a squat warm-ivory ceramic robot with a softly rounded trapezoid body, inset graphite face with two simple expressive cream eyes and mouth, moss-green side panels, a single short bent terracotta antenna, little articulated mitten hands and stubby feet. It feels like a small expressive couch buddy, not an assistant logo.
Pose language: WATCHING leans toward the game with keen interest; HYPED throws hands up with a wide happy mouth; SKEPTICAL gives an affectionate raised-brow side-eye; OOPS is sheepish with hands raised defensively and a tiny plain helmet tilted askew. Vary body language as well as faces. Every row keeps exactly the same character anatomy and materials across all four poses.
Style/medium: premium hand-crafted 2.5D character development art, tactile matte clay and felt materials, simple bold silhouettes, crisp controlled outlines, subtle soft contact shadows, restrained shading, charming expressive face animation potential. Not shiny plastic and not photorealism.
Composition/framing: ample ivory negative space, 3 rows x 4 poses aligned on a precise grid, all characters full-body and unobstructed, enough room between poses for each silhouette. Strong editorial title at top left "A friend for the run". Small line beneath "Project Couch / Character exploration". Small but readable footer "VISUAL CONCEPT · ORIGINAL CHARACTER STUDIES".
Color palette: warm paper ivory #F3F0E7, graphite #29332F, muted moss #74816B, terracotta #C77B58. No neon, no purple gradients.
Typography: clean intentional humanist sans serif, clear large column and row labels, generous spacing, exactly spelled text.
Constraints: entire image is the board itself with no surrounding desk or device. Exactly three distinct designs, twelve character poses total. No existing game characters, no Pokemon, no Glimlet, no OpenAI branding, no real platform logos, no watermarks. Project Couch is only a temporary project label. These are illustrative concepts, not a working app.
stream:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: landscape Twitch-stream-style composition illustrating an original screen-aware gameplay companion.
Primary request: Create a polished wide landscape 3:2 visual concept of a stream, with a broad original gameplay scene occupying almost all the canvas and a compact expressive companion anchored safely near the lower-left corner. Use the exact POCKET BOT design from row 03 of the supplied character sheet as the companion identity; do not reproduce the sheet or other characters.
Scene/background: beautiful generic original isometric adventure gameplay, a small caped explorer stands at the edge of a broken mossy stone bridge over a misty forest ravine, distant windmills and soft late-afternoon light. A plainly visible broken section of bridge is the situation the companion is reacting to. Entirely original environment and player, not any existing game. The hero and traversal action are mid-frame toward the right, far from overlay. Subtle readable game HUD at upper left with three small health pips and a simple short objective at upper right "Cross the old bridge". No elaborate borders. Rich atmospheric art with legible navigable terrain, restrained natural greens and blue-grey shadows.
Companion: consistent ivory ceramic POCKET BOT with graphite inset expressive face, moss side panels, one bent terracotta antenna, mitten hands and stubby feet, now wearing a tiny plain helmet tilted slightly. Companion fully visible in lower-left, about 14 percent of image height and 9 percent of image width, front-facing three-quarter view, giving the streamer an amused skeptical side-eye while gesturing at the gap in the bridge. It sits over the game with a soft local shadow, no large webcam rectangle, no support dashboard, no background card behind character.
Caption: a single compact warm-ivory speech bubble placed just above and to the right of the bot, very legible graphite humanist sans serif text EXACTLY "We can make that. Probably." No other companion speech. Small tail points to the bot. Bubble must not cover the player, the bridge gap, objective or health. This is an affectionate spontaneous backseat moment.
Composition/framing: full-bleed gameplay, game-first. Small dark translucent top-left stream label "Project Couch" with a subtle red dot and "LIVE CONCEPT". At upper right beneath game objective, a modest two-line viewer chat overlay with text "fern: trust the helmet" and "lofi: here we go again". Place chat in quiet sky area. Footer in subtle small legible text "ILLUSTRATIVE STREAM MOCKUP". No sidebars, giant UI panels, desktop window, fake app frame or marketing headline.
Style/medium: high-quality stylized 2.5D original adventure screenshot concept with a hand-crafted character overlay; deliberate interface spacing and crisp typography. Friendly, relaxed, quietly funny.
Constraints: game action dominates more than 85% of visual area; preserve compact companion, clear focus, and readable short caption. No Glimlet, Pokemon, existing game characters, OpenAI branding or real platform logos. Project Couch only a temporary label. This image illustrates a proposed experience, not footage from a working application.
creator:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: polished desktop creator and control screen concept for Project Couch, a screen-aware gameplay entertainment companion.
Primary request: one extremely clear, believable desktop application UI shown straight-on and filling a landscape 3:2 canvas, with a warm editorial light theme and thoughtful functional controls. Use the exact POCKET BOT design in row 03 of the supplied character sheet for the character preview; do not reproduce the sheet. This original robot has ivory ceramic rounded trapezoid body, graphite inset face, cream animated eyes and mouth, muted moss side panels, a single bent terracotta antenna, mitten hands and stubby feet.
Layout: one quiet full-width top bar. Left reads "Project Couch" with a small sublabel "Concept". Right has a green status dot, "OBS connected", and a restrained solid moss-green "Start session" button. Under it, a slim left navigation rail about 13 percent width with text items "Companion" (selected), "Session", "Memories", "Connections". Main area title "Make yourself a couch buddy" and a short muted subtitle "A little character. A lot of opinions."
Main area uses three intentional panels with ample whitespace. Left preview panel approximately 30% of usable width: heading "Character"; a large clean preview of the happy POCKET BOT on soft ivory with tiny ground shadow, several small expression thumbnail controls below for idle, happy and skeptical, plus buttons "Try a line" and "Change character". No huge decorative illustration, preview stays inside its panel. Under preview a compact "Stream preview" area showing original mossy bridge gameplay and the same tiny bot at its lower-left, so screen awareness is visually present.
Middle settings panel approximately 34% width, titled "Personality". Clearly aligned real controls: a "Name" field with placeholder "Name your buddy"; a "Voice" dropdown displaying "Warm & wry" and small play audition icon; a "Personality" segmented choice with "Playful" selected and other options "Chill" and "Bold"; a short text description "A loyal friend with questionable confidence."; a "Talkativeness" horizontal slider at a moderate setting, endpoints "Quiet" and "Chatty"; a separate "Backseating" slider slightly above middle, endpoints "Gentle" and "Unfiltered"; a toggle row "Give me room to focus" set ON. Keep every label and control spaced, aligned and highly readable.
Right session panel approximately 36% width, titled "Watch with me". A "Game" dropdown displaying "Mossbridge demo"; a "Screen source" dropdown displaying "Game Capture"; a "Microphone" dropdown displaying "Default microphone"; a "Twitch chat" row with green dot and "Connected"; a "Look up game mechanics" toggle ON; a "Spoilers" dropdown displaying "No story spoilers". An inset small OBS section reads "OBS Studio" and "Overlay connected", with an "Open overlay" button. Bottom session status strip has three small green-dot items "Seeing game", "Hearing you", "Reading chat".
Text note at the very bottom of canvas "ILLUSTRATIVE UI CONCEPT · PROJECT NAME IS TEMPORARY". Clear crisp typography with enough size to read at normal presentation size, sentence case, no tiny body paragraphs. Controls should look usable and purposeful rather than decorative.
Style/medium: refined contemporary desktop product design, humanist sans serif, warm paper #F3F0E7 background, nearly white panels, deep graphite #29332F type, moss-green #74816B selected states and primary action, terracotta #C77B58 character accents, subtle thin dividers, very light shadows, modest corner radii. No neon, purple gradients, glossy glass, stock dashboard charts or unnecessary decoration.
Constraints: all requested fields visible at once, no overlaps, no cut-off controls, no lorem ipsum, no product name other than temporary Project Couch. No Glimlet, Pokemon, existing game characters, OpenAI branding or real platform logos. OBS and Twitch may appear as plain-text connection labels. Show an illustrative design, not a claim that the software currently works.
